[USER] User inquired about typical Italian breakfast dishes enjoyed by locals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some typical Italian breakfast dishes include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Cappuccino and cornetto (an Italian croissant)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Frittata (an open-faced omelette with vegetables and/or meat)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Tiramisu (yes, Italians do eat dessert for breakfast!)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Toast with Nutella or jam  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Yogurt with granola and fruit  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Panini with cheese and prosciutto  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Pastries such as sfogliatelle, babka or brioche  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Eggs Benedict Italian style with ham and hollandaise sauce.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Note: Breakfast culture in Italy varies; some Italians might just have a coffee or espresso with some biscuits or bread.

[USER] User asked if Italians drink orange juice for breakfast.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Orange juice is not a popular breakfast drink in Italy as it is in other countries like the United States.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Italian breakfast is more focused on coffee drinks like cappuccino or espresso, and pastries or bread.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is not uncommon for Italians to consume some fresh fruit or juice as part of their breakfast.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some Italians might enjoy orange juice in the morning, but it is not a traditional or typical Italian breakfast choice.
